thread:
mina: quick follow-up from the offload RFC — i sketched a 'soft-hand' ownership model for GPU<->host pages, want opinions before i put it in an RFC update
jon: nice, high level?
mina: idea: instead of strict move semantics, we give pages a lease + soft-hand flag. owner can 'soft-hand' a page to the other side with a lease duration and a fallback contract. if the receiver needs it urgently, they can take ownership early but must satisfy fallback recovery steps. avoids synchronous handshakes for common case
peggy: can you sketch the API? how do we avoid races where two sides think they own it?
mina: minimal API proposal:
```
soft_hand(page_id, to=HOST|GPU, lease_ms=200, fallback=RETURN|RECLAIM) -> lease_token
claim(page_id, lease_token) -> ok|conflict
release(page_id, lease_token)
query_owner(page_id) -> {owner, lease_expiry}
```
peggy: hmm so claim could race but the token ensures we know who initiated. what about pinned pages and mmap'd host backing?
alex: pinned pages should be excluded from soft-hand unless explicitly allowed by the allocator. we need a policy: pinned->no-soft-hand, staging->allowed, mmap-backed->only if host cooperates (can't silently evict)
ryan: fallback semantics matter a lot. RETURN vs RECLAIM are different cost profiles. RETURN asks receiver to push back; RECLAIM forces a copy/serialize back to origin. i worry about latent reclaim cost impacting latency SLOs
mina: agreed. default should be RETURN, RECLAIM only for low-latency background paths. we also need an asynchronous reclaim channel that returns a promise/handle so requesters can wait or proceed with degraded plan
jon: telemetry: we should tag each soft-hand with reason tags (prefetch, eviction, compaction) so we can measure how often claim happens early and cost distributions
peggy: and a per-tenant opt-in for aggressive reclaim; enterprise customers might prefer deterministic reclaim behavior in Dedicated/private deployments
mina: good call. also adding a 'grace window' where the original owner will honor lightweight reads (read-only) while lease active to reduce churn for small reads
alex: race handling detail: when claim conflict occurs, return structured conflict including current owner lease_expiry + suggested backoff. avoid blocking callers; let runtime retry with jitter
ryan: do we need kernel-level hooks or can this live purely in runtime/user-space? for mmap'd host pages kernel cooperation is needed for eviction notifications
mina: plan: implement runtime-only prototype using explicit host <-> agent RPC for host-managed pages. keep kernel hook path for later (v2) where we can subscribe to mmu notifiers. prototype will use agent ack + best-effort pin checks
peggy: what about compaction and fragmentation? if soft-hands proliferate, compaction might be constantly fighting leases. need compaction-aware lease acquisition that can request 'grant-exception' windows
mina: yep: compaction controller will use a 'compaction_swap_preempt' flag that requests short exclusive leases (e.g., 50ms) and global backoff if too many outstanding exceptions
jon: could we prioritize by hotness score? i.e., when offering soft-hand, include a hotness hint so the receiver can decide to accept or decline to avoid thrashing
mina: yes include hotness_hint in API. runtime will use it to decide whether to claim or immediately return
infra-bot: deploy-check: gating files changed: runtime/allocator/soft_hand.proto, runtime/evictor/policy.md (2 files). CI: ok
ryan: testing: we should add microbench: claim-latency distribution, reclaim-cost p50/p95, compaction-failure rate. run with synthetic mixed workload (inference + embedding)
peggy: also subscribe to tenant-level metrics: lease-frequencies, cross-node hand rates, reclaim-bytes/sec. add SLA alerts if reclaim-bytes/sec > threshold
mina: next steps: i'll add RFC update with the API + proto + telemetry plan. will include a small emulation script for early perf numbers. any objections to the approach?
jon: fine with me. add explicit 'no-soft-hand' allocation flag for embed/pinned allocs
alex: yep + document kernel-path as future work
peggy: nit: make lease_token opaque and rotateable (avoid reuse confusions)
mina: noted. thanks all — i'll drop a draft later today and ping for reviews :thumbsup:
